title: Two-color solitons in Kerr third harmonic generation model
authors: Alexey Sukhinin, Curtis Menyuk, Natalia Litchinitser, Jean-Claude Diels, Alejandro B Aceves
abstract: We investigate two-color, two dimensional spatially localized light modes in a resonant Kerr third-harmonic generation model. Using computational tools, we identify two distinct families of localized states. Unlike the single-component 2D nonlinear Schrödinger equation and previously studied non-resonant two-color systems, the dynamics are not dictated by a universal critical power, but depend on the distribution of power between the harmonics. The "fundamental-dominated" family acts as a "dynamical separatrix" between simultaneous collapse and joint diffraction, whereas the "third-harmonic-dominated" family does not. We further identify resonant collapse events accompanied by strong oscillations of the third harmonic, revealing a collapse mechanism absent from standard Kerr self-focusing.
summary: This paper analyzes two-color solitons in a resonant Kerr third-harmonic generation medium. The research identifies two distinct families of localized states whose stability and collapse behavior depend critically on the relative power between the fundamental and third harmonic components. By simulating perturbations, the authors reveal novel collapse mechanisms absent in standard self-focusing theories.
main_problem: The study investigates two-color, two-dimensional spatially localized light modes (solitons) within a resonant Kerr third-harmonic generation model.
main_result: Two distinct families of solitons exist whose dynamics are governed by the relative power distribution between harmonics, showing that no universal critical collapse power exists.
method: The authors employed numerical methods, including solving coupled nonlinear equations for stationary states and performing direct time-domain simulations using pseudo-spectral Fourier techniques on perturbed solutions.
model_or_system: The system is a resonant Kerr third-harmonic generation (THG) model involving two interacting color beams ($\omega_1$ and $2\omega_1$), described by coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equations.
key_observables: Individual component powers ($P_1, P_2$), total power, linear stability spectrum eigenvalues, and the evolution of field amplitudes during propagation (collapse vs. diffraction).
important_parameters: The ratio of power between the fundamental and third harmonic components ($P_1$ vs $P_2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a quasi-monochromatic approximation and assumes the existence of stationary solutions which are then perturbed for dynamic study.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate representative localized states, stability spectra for different power regimes, and time evolution profiles showing collapse dynamics preceded by strong third-harmonic oscillations in certain families.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving the coupled nonlinear equations, numerically finding two distinct stationary soliton families based on power distribution, and then simulating perturbations around these states to characterize their stability and collapse behavior.
why_interesting: This work explores complex nonlinear wave dynamics in a resonant optical system, providing insights into non-standard self-focusing mechanisms that deviate from single-component models, which is relevant for understanding energy localization in nonlinear media.
